name: HubSpot Service Hub
oneLiner: Customer service software on the HubSpot CRM: help desk, tickets, knowledge base, customer portal, feedback surveys and the Breeze Customer Agent AI.
bestFor: Teams that already use HubSpot for marketing or sales and want support conversations on the same customer record.

customers.name: Twelve (ordering and payments app; partner case study)

updates.text: Breeze Customer Agent made available to all Pro and Enterprise customers across hubs through HubSpot Credits, covering the whole buyer journey; HubSpot said it helped customers resolve over 50% of support tickets.
Help desk gained assignment-workflow routing (e.g. VIP or language-based routing, conditional Customer Agent handoffs) and a Coaching Opportunities page for Customer Agent.

From April 14, 2026, Breeze Customer Agent moved to outcome-based pricing: $0.50 per resolved conversation (was $1.00 per conversation). HubSpot said it resolves 65% of conversations across more than 8,000 customers who activated it; available to Pro and Enterprise customers.

features: Help desk workspace for email, chat, WhatsApp, Facebook Messenger and calling channels
Breeze Customer Agent AI that answers from your knowledge base and hands off to people
Knowledge base and customer portal for self-service
Ticket routing, SLAs and automation workflows
NPS, CSAT and CES feedback surveys
Every conversation logged on the shared HubSpot CRM record

pricing.text: Free tools for up to 2 users. Paid plans per seat per month: Starter lists at $20/seat/month (HubSpot's catalog), with new-customer promotions (the pricing page showed $7/seat/month on an annual commitment); Professional $90/seat/month billed annually ($100 paid monthly) plus a required one-time $1,500 onboarding fee; Enterprise from $150/seat/month plus a required one-time $3,500 onboarding fee. 14-day free trial. Included HubSpot Credits: 500 (Starter), 3,000 (Professional), 5,000 (Enterprise); extra credits $0.010 each.

notes: hubspot.com could not be fetched; prices come from search snippets of the official page. Starter price conflicts across sources ($7, $15, $20 per seat), so the review doesn't quote it. The original's $15/seat Starter price was dropped. Calling channel requires Professional or Enterprise. Twelve is a partner-written (Webs) case study. November 2026: hubspot.com/pricing/service fetched directly; it shows Starter at $7 and $20, Professional at $90 and $100, with 'Discounts available for new customers only'. HubSpot's search snippet maps $7 to a promotional annual price against a normal $20, and the Products & Services Catalog lists Starter from $20 per Core Seat, so the review quotes $20. Knowledge base is Professional and Enterprise only (hubspot.com/products/service/knowledge-base). G2 rating from a search snippet of the G2 reviews page (4.4 from 3,016; the G2 pricing page showed 2,917).
pros: Shared CRM record: support conversations sit on the same HubSpot record as marketing and sales activity
Free tools for up to 2 users and a 14-day free trial of paid plans
Breeze Customer Agent answers from your knowledge base; HubSpot says it resolves 65% of conversations (April 2026)
Many channels in one help desk: email, chat, WhatsApp, Facebook Messenger and calling
Built-in NPS, CSAT and CES surveys

cons.text: Required one-time onboarding fees: $1,500 for Professional and $3,500 for Enterprise
The knowledge base isn't in Free or Starter; it needs Professional or Enterprise
Customer Agent needs Professional or Enterprise and is billed per resolved conversation ($0.50) through HubSpot Credits
Built around the HubSpot CRM, so teams whose customer data lives in another CRM get less from the shared record
A general customer service help desk: replying to public reviews on Google or Yelp needs another tool
